All credit for this goes to GloriousEggroll at reddit. Posting here because it's the most comprehensive guide I've seen to running in Linux. Original post is here: https://www.reddit.com/r/ffxiv/comments/3al9na/psa_ffxiv_linux_winestaging/

Before this gets flagged, let me clarify that WINE is a linux program designed to allow linux users to run their windows software in linux. Wine-staging, is a series of direct3d patches made to wine, so that games and applications run smoother as if running natively in windows. It is not a 3rd party program nor does it modify the program itself in any way.

Moving on:

Hi everyone, just wanted to let those interested know that FFXIV: Heavensward runs beautifully on linux using wine-staging with 1 Minor detail. I'm not sure if this is applicable to all, but HDR Rendering when enabled causes a crash for me. If I leave it normal I can run everything else cranked all the way up on my GTX 680.

Details:

Using:
Arch Linux x86_64 rolling release 6-1-2015
Wine 1.7.45 with CSMT/wine-staging patches
NVIDIA GTX 680 with latest drivers from official arch repos (Driver Version: 352.09)

Instructions:

PART 1: Getting wine with csmt patches installed

Arch linux

In arch from AUR Repos:

Easy way: 

yaourt -S wine-staging

gives you 1.7.44-1 with CSMT patches

Better way:
Download the wine-staging tarball and extract it somewhere, edit PKGBUILD to version 1.7.45 (latest version), run it once, (it will error out due to mismatched md5sum, thats ok). You can download the tarball here:
https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/wine-staging/

You should now have wine-1.7.45.tar.gz and v1.7.45.tar.gz (or something similar) in your extracted wine-staging folder. Do the following in terminal in that folder: 

md5sum wine-1.7.45.tar.gz
md5sum v1.7.45.tar.gz

new md5 codes should be spit out for you to add to the pkgbuild file.

Back in the PKGBUILD, edit the first two md5 lines with the new ones.
In the wine-staging folder, delete previous pkg and src folders if they were generated. You may have to delete pkg as root/sudo using 

sudo rm -R pkg
sudo rm -R src

NOW in terminal go to the wine-staging folder and 

makepkg

then 

sudo pacman -U the-new.pkg.tar.gz

to install the latest and greatest wine with csmt/staging

Ubuntu:

http://www.ubuntuupdates.org/package/ehoover_compholio_netflix/trusty/main/base/wine-staging

PART 2: Configuring wine to work with CSMT patches

In terminal: 

WINEARCH=win32 WINEPREFIX=~/.wine32-ffxiv winecfg

go to staging tab. check the CSMT box. Close the config.

In terminal: 

WINEARCH=win32 WINEPREFIX=~/.wine32-ffxiv winetricks d3dx9 devenum ie8 quartz wininet winhttp xact_jun2010 wmp10

Next, copy this and save it as whateversomename.reg: 

[HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Wine\Direct3D] 
"CSMT"="enabled" 

[HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Wine\Direct3D] 
"StrictDrawOrdering"="disabled" 

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\CLSID\{7D8AA343-6E63-4663-BE90-6B80F66540A3}] 
@="VMR ImageSync" 

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\CLSID\{7D8AA343-6E63-4663-BE90-6B80F66540A3}\InprocServer32] 
@="C:\\WINDOWS\\system32\\quartz.dll" 
"ThreadingModel"="Both" 

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\CLSID\{99D54F63-1A69-41AE-AA4D-C976EB3F0713}] 
@="VMR Allocator Presenter" 

[HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\CLSID\{99D54F63-1A69-41AE-AA4D-C976EB3F0713}\InprocServer32] 
@="C:\\WINDOWS\\system32\\quartz.dll" 
"ThreadingModel"="Both"

In terminal: 

WINEARCH=win32 WINEPREFIX=~/.wine32-ffxiv regedit

File>Import registry file
Navigate to and choose the whateversomename.reg we just made.
Close regedit.

PART 3: RUN THE GAME!

Create a start script, I named mine ffxiv.sh: 

#!/bin/sh

export WINEARCH=win32
export WINEPREFIX=~/.wine32-ffxiv
export CSMT=enabled

# COMMENT IF THE GAME IS FAILING TO LAUNCH
export WINEDEBUG=-all

# UNCOMMENT THESE LINES IF YOU USE NVIDIA DRIVERS
export LD_PRELOAD="libpthread.so.0 libGL.so.1"
export __GL_THREADED_OPTIMISATIONS=1

# UNCOMMENT THESE FOR VSYNC. 
export __GL_SYNC_TO_VBLANK=1

# Note IF RUNNING DUAL MONITORS WITH VSYNC: 
#You must open your X log in /var/logs and find which display port your game monitor is on. (mine was DFP-0)
#Then set the appropriate device in the line below and uncomment
#export __GL_SYNC_DISPLAY_DEVICE=DFP-0

#this path works for arch, not sure of the ubuntu path
WINE=/bin/wine


$WINE "/your/ffxiv/absolute/game/path/boot/ffxivboot.exe"

Then

chmod a+x launchscriptname.sh
./launchscriptname.sh

After the game launches, double check to make sure the launcher still isnt running in the background as for some reason it can eat quite a bit of resources.

sudo killall -9 ffxivlauncher.exe

PART 4: IN-GAME SETTINGS

Before you even press -start game- there are a few settings you need to enable/disable, so as soon as the game loads up, click configuration on the main menu and set these settings. Without them, you -will- get crashes. I tested settings over 3 days and these were needed in order for the game not to crash.

Under the Graphics Settings section:
[DISABLED] Enable HDR rendering and improve overall graphics quality.
[ENABLED] Disable rendering of objects when not visible. (Occlusion Culling)
[ENABLED] Use low-detail models on distant objects (LOD).
[ENABLED] Cache LOD data only when necessary. (LOD Streaming)
[ENABLED] Use low-detail models on shadows. (LOD)
[Normal - 1024p] Shadow Resolution

All other graphics settings can be cranked up or tuned down as much as you want

It fell; a mountain of of sillicate dropped like so many sacks of potatoes. Like a child in a sandbox, the asteroid fell with a thud and a circular spray. Unlike a a child's shenanigans, this thud alone sent a shockwave through thousands of kilometers of what used to be the Northeast border between Canada and the US. This wave, a moving mortared wall, passed right on through the both strong concrete of our homes and buildings and the weak skin, scales, fur and flesh of those that populated our sad little blue planet. It liquefied these poor souls in an instant moving faster than the speed of sound. That was only the beginning. At this point, there was nothing to do but watch the disaster unfold.

The spray, a column of dirt, dust, and rock embedded with the odd car, house, and freeway flew to hundreds of feet high, and then fell like so many stars. How beautiful it was, looking down inside the safety of an orbiting spaceship. How terrible it was, at ground zero. This ring of ejected meteorites burned twice as bright for half as long. The atmosphere was too dense for them to live for very long, and they melted and crystallized into a glass that hailed arrowheads onto the ground. Ever wonder how we figured out that the dinosaurs were an extinct species? The rock layer that covers the world. Everywhere you turned, there would be this thin band. We can even see it nowadays, if you dug a little. I mean, we could have, had the world not just been sledgehammered by a space rock, adding another layer to our pockmarked collection.

As you looked further up the impact, from the point where giant crater met embedded space debris to the now empty sky above it, it only got worse. The asteroid had impacted so quickly that the atmosphere behind it had been punctured like a bike tire, except instead of air rushing out, the cold vacuum of space rushed to meet it's new emptiness. This cold, a type of frozen dipping to a temperature so low in fact, that we struggle to even maintain anything near it for any amount of time. A whopping 0K, if you in ideal conditions. That cold in a laboratory? Chilly. That cold over an entire hurricane - spanning super-storm; deadly. To nearly everything.

As depressing as it is thinking about it so soon after, not everyone died an equal death. Not in the philosophical bullshit morality kind of way; I mean in pure degrees of pain. There are the early casualties. Dead so quickly there wasn't even concrete to burn a shadow into. They were the lucky ones. There were those who would die from the cold. Not like in the starving for food type of death (that would come later), but more of an instantaneous deep freeze. Sort of like putting a banana in liquid nitrogen. Exactly like the wasteland in Snowpiercer, without the hopeful ending. Damn, I'm never going to see a movie again.

Those "fortunate" to be far enough underground to avoid the atmospheric maelstrom were spared from instant death. Most considered it a curse. Food ran out first. Even on strict rations, there was only so much to go around. Hard decision were made. Those who elected to live were the useful ones: electricians, doctors, plumbers, and the young and healthy. Someone had to live in the shitty world, might as well be the ones who could make it. Man, do I wish I was with them. We knew the communication was going to be severed between the ground and us soon after initial impact. Every physicist with a telescope had been tracking, measuring and simulating every possible situation. Between 19:37 and 19:61, July 1st 2036, Apophis would travel along its orbit around the Sun, bringing it a measly 10 000 kilometers from the Earth, well within the Clarke orbit range. If they were alive right now, they'd be pretty happy to know they were right! Good for them. Gold stickers all around.

Only if there had been enough time. No one believed it could happen until it actually was. It's been nearly a century since the first atomic bombs were detonated, and we hadn't improved on it since. All we could do was put a lot of fissile materials in one place. So here we are, eh? Sitting strapped to the world's largest nuke while the thing we were supposed to deflect zipped right past us so quickly it was gone before initiation sequence could even begin. Kind of a bummer. No one specific is to blame, really. It was something humanity had to do as a whole, and just couldn't make it work in time. Oh well.

All in all, we're an awfully resilient species. There are 11 of us on the ship with me, experts in our own useful ways. We came prepared even for this sad outcome. We were loaded food, water, oxygen, and CO2 scrubbers to last at least us a few generations. We had the means to live up here for god damn long time. Hopefully enough to figure out this mess. We're human. We're survivors.
